title: Silverfold Commerce outbound draft — discovery + objection flows
content:
Account snapshot:
- Company: Silverfold Commerce (mid-market e-commerce platform focused on niche home goods). Estimated org size: 300–600 employees. US & EU presence, fulfillment in US.
- Tech stack signals: modern infra (Kubernetes on AWS), heavy usage of Redis for session/caching, Kafka for event streams. Open-source models in experiments (internal slack chatter referencing LLaMA fine-tuning).
- Why they matter: active personalization roadmap (recommendation + cross-sell), merchants complaining about search latency when traffic spikes. They run in multiple regions and care about predictable latencies for checkout related features.

Hypothesis / value props to test:
1) Predictable latency and throughput for customer-facing personalization and search ranking (reduce p95 from ~800ms to <200ms).
2) Lower per-token cost on re-ranking/batch-embedding workloads via batching + KV cache.
3) Private tenant option: Silverfold likely needs data isolation for merchant PII; Redwood Private + KMS integration is relevant.

Key stakeholders to reach (mapped):
- VP Engineering: Marco Valdez — owns platform reliability and infra spend
- Head of ML / ML Platform: Aisha Patel — owns model infra, onboarding new models, latency targets
- CTO: Renee Salazar — strategic buyer for platform choices, compliance guardrails
- Eng Manager (Search): Ben Chu — daily pain owner (p95 search latency spikes)

Signals to mention in outreach:
- "We noticed a public issue thread about search latency (Nov 2025) and a Slack post about LLaMA experiments — seems like a fit for lower-latency serving with model rollouts."
- Billing/ops: they use reserved EC2+spot mix — interest in predictable throughput pricing for peak holiday traffic.

Outbound email draft (cold — short):
Subject: Cut search p95 during peaks for Silverfold merchants
Hi Marco —
I’m Priya on the Redwood Inference GTM team. Noticed Silverfold’s recent notes about search latency and LLaMA experiments — would love to share a short case on how customers reduced p95 from ~800ms to sub-200ms using a dedicated inference layer (and got predictable costs during peak traffic).
2 options: quick 15m intro this week, or I can send a 1-page ROI snapshot. Which works?
— Priya

Follow-up (if no response):
Subject: Quick ROI for search re-ranking at Silverfold
Marco — following up — attached a 60s read showing throughput & cost improvements (example: 30% per-token cost reduction vs naive cloud endpoints using batching + KV cache). Want me to put together numbers using your Q4 holiday traffic?

Outbound email draft (to Aisha / ML platform):
Subject: low-friction model rollouts & canarying for Silverfold’s LLaMA experiments
Aisha —
We built model rollouts + automatic fallback policies so product teams can test new model variants without risking checkout latency. If you have 20m this week I can show how we do canary + A/B with traceable quality regressions against a prompt set.

Call script / discovery checklist (15m):
- 0–2m: intro, quick context why we reached out (search + personalization pain).
- 2–6m: current infra — where do you host models (managed endpoints, k8s, on-prem?), typical seq lengths and p95 today for search/re-ranking?
- 6–10m: volumes — avg tokens per request, peak qps during promos/holiday, % reranking vs generation.
- 10–12m: risk & compliance — merchant PII handling, encryption/KMS, audit log requirements.
- 12–15m: success criteria for a pilot (latency target, cost saving, safety/regression thresholds).
- Next steps: propose pilot: 4-week pilot, one route (re-ranking for top-10 results) with canary and rollback; brief ROI estimate.

Objection map (common + suggested replies):
- "We host everything in AWS managed endpoints already."
  Reply: "Totally common — Redwood is designed to plug into your infra (dedicated pools or private deployments). We can run in your VPC and hand off traffic with the same SDK; most teams start with a small canary route to compare p95/cost side-by-side."

- "We built an internal inference layer; switching is risky."
  Reply: "Understand. We can run a non-invasive side-by-side pilot (shadow traffic + metrics) and show identical API surface so your engineers keep their existing calls while we collect latency/cost deltas. Also offer model pinning and rollback: zero-risk from a user-facing standpoint."

- "Cost — we think clouds are cheaper for our scale."
  Reply: "We typically beat vanilla managed endpoints once you account for tail latency, autoscaling inefficiencies, and lack of batching. We’ll model your Q4 traffic to estimate per-request savings (no charge for that estimate)."

- "Data security / compliance concerns for merchant data."
  Reply: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs. For many enterprise customers we can demonstrate a compliance runbook and an isolated control plane that meets SOC2-style requirements."

Quick technical notes to prep for demo (internal):
- Need sample traffic profile: typical seq lengths (search reranker ~128 tokens), batchability window tolerance (50–200ms), pkgs per second at peak.
- Prepare a replay pipeline: use their reranking logs to replay into Redwood and capture p95 comparisons. Ask infra for a short export or provide instructions for a small replay job.
- Evaluate if quantized variants would be beneficial — auto-suggestion: 8-bit quantization + KV cache for reranking workload.

Open questions (for Aisha / Ben):
- Do you have hard SLOs for search p95 tied to merchant SLAs?
- Which environment would you prefer for a pilot: hosted-proxy vs private VPC?
- Any internal legal/regulatory redlines (specific merchants that require stricter controls)?

To dos (next 7 days):
- Draft 1-pager ROI for Marco (Ethan to help with sample numbers) — due 03/04.
- Ask Zara to map existing Slack mentions & public threads we can cite — due 03/03.
- Create a minimal replay script template (Python) and include instructions for k8s job — Priya — due 03/05.
- Schedule discovery: try Marco Thurs 3/5 10am PT — tentative.

Notes to self (tone / approach):
- Keep first email short and outcome-oriented (quick intro + clear next step).
- Avoid starting with technical deep-dive — surface pain and ROI early.
- For Aisha: bring demo of canary + auto-rollback and prompt-set regression examples.

Random scratch thoughts (brain dump):
- Potential pilot route: re-ranking for logged-in personalized results (less risk than checkout).
- In outreach, call out holiday traffic as a proxy for their worst-case to get attention.
- Might offer a small credit for a side-by-side replay (to reduce friction).

History / previous touches: none (cold). No current vendor listed in public docs.

End of doc — quick checklist before send:
- [ ] ROI 1-pager attached
- [ ] Replay instructions cleaned
- [ ] Slack thread with warm intros (if any) linked in the outreach
